questions.cardText:
[Earth Science] What inorganic molecule is produced by lightning?
A. Ozone (O₃)
B. Methane (CH₄)
C. Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)
Answer: A. Known to be “good up high, but bad nearby,” ozone in the stratosphere is beneficial, protecting life on Earth from excessive UV radiation, but at ground level, it is a harmful air pollutant.
questions.de: Welche Form des Sauerstoffs – „oben gut, unten schlecht“ – entsteht durch Blitze und verleiht der Luft nach einem Einschlag ihren stechenden Geruch?
questions.en: Which form of oxygen – “good up high, but bad nearby” – is produced by lightning and gives the air its sharp smell after a strike?

timeline.labelEn: Christian Friedrich Schönbein isolates the gas he smelled after lightning and names it ozone
timeline.labelDe: Christian Friedrich Schönbein isoliert das nach Blitzen gerochene Gas und nennt es Ozon

questions.notes: Card correct. Lightning also produces large amounts of nitrogen oxides (NOx, ~7 kg per flash), so the question is anchored on the oxygen form/smell to keep one answer. Timeline from the Ozone article (named 1839).

questions.cardText:
[Zoology] What is the shape of the African lungfish?
A. Streamlined and elongated
B. Round and flat
C. Short and stubby
Answer: A. Despite being a fish, the African lungfish can drown if it does not have access to air, as it primarily relies on its lungs to breathe atmospheric oxygen.
questions.de: Welche Körperform hat der Afrikanische Lungenfisch – ein Fisch, der ohne Zugang zur Luft ertrinken kann?
questions.en: What body shape does the African lungfish – a fish that can drown without access to air – have?

timeline.labelEn: Richard Owen describes Protopterus, the genus of the African lungfishes
timeline.labelDe: Richard Owen beschreibt Protopterus, die Gattung der Afrikanischen Lungenfische

questions.notes: Card correct: Wikipedia says African lungfish are elongated, eel-like, and obligate air breathers.
